claim: Highlight reformulations, require confirmation for ambiguous acronyms and always display reference date and source version.
I would add a dedicated bilingual test before promoting any normalizer to production.
Eighteen internal users participated over two weeks. Eighty-three percent correctly identified the current source, and 78 percent understood when a query had been reformulated.
In six cases, users accepted an incorrect acronym expansion because the interface did not highlight the change strongly enough.
The experimental branch improves recall on the typographical stress set from 72.9 to 77.6 percent, but loses two points on queries containing proper names.
